earlier_scan.note: Extinct; only 19th-c. wordlists (Jardine 1886, MacGillivray 1852, Ray 1907) and comparative notes; no phonological description

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1907. Reports of the Cambridge Anthropological Expedition to Torres Straits, Vol. III: Linguistics. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. Gudang at pp. 264-265 (history of the lists), 281-283 ('A short comparative vocabulary of the languages of Cape York Peninsula'), 512-513 (conclusions).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ray says the Gudang material (Jukes, MacGillivray, Murray, Jardine) gave no 'sufficient indication of the structure of the languages' and that in 1898 Jardine reported the language 'practically extinct'; the Gudang column is a comparative wordlist only. The one 'accented syllables' remark (p. 6) belongs to the Mabuiag/Western Torres Strait phonology, not Gudang.

sources.citation: Jardine, Frank L. 1886. 'No. 7 — Cape York: The Gudang tribe', pp. 278-283 in E. M. Curr, The Australian Race, Vol. II. Melbourne: Government Printer.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Short ethnographic note (tribe 'now nearly extinct') plus a Cape York / Erroob-Masseed comparative wordlist; no pronunciation or accent remark at all.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2012. Change Request 2012-053: create [xgd] Gudang. SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Administrative; sources named are Austlang, Bowern's databases, Tindale 1974, Hercus 1969; no linguistic description.

sources.citation: Wikipedia contributors. 'Gudang language' (phonology and Gudang-vs-Urradhi sections drawn from Rod Mitchell's reconstruction of the MacGillivray/Brierly material; cites Mitchell 1995, Moore 1979, Dixon 2002, Crowley 1983).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Reconstructed consonant and vowel inventories and sound correspondences with Urradhi (38% shared cognates, 'a separate language from the Urradhi group'); no statement on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Crowley, Terry. 1983. 'Uradhi', pp. 306-428 in R.M.W. Dixon & B.J. Blake (eds), Handbook of Australian Languages, Vol. 3. Canberra: ANU Press. (p. 306 lists 'kuta (Jardine's Gudang, Meston's Gootung, Sharp's Gudang) - Somerset' among local groups of the yumukuɲji cluster; 2.3 Stress p. 322.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: States the Uradhi rule ('Primary stress is placed on the antepenultimate syllable.. of a word that contains only short vowels.. long vowels.. receive primary stress, regardless of their position') with Atampaya examples, prefaced 'The stress rules throughout the Uradhi dialects appear to be fairly uniform'. Crowley had no Gudang data (extinct); the rule is not attributed to Gudang here.

sources.citation: Hale, Kenneth L. 1964. Classification of Northern Paman languages, Cape York Peninsula, Australia: a research report. Oceanic Linguistics 3(2): 248-265.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative/classificatory; Glottolog cites p. 252 for Gudang's subclassification; no stress expected.

sources.citation: MacGillivray, John. 1852. Narrative of the voyage of H.M.S. Rattlesnake, Vol. II, Appendix: Vocabulary of the Australians of Cape York (Gudang) and Kowrarega, pp. 277-316, with Latham's remarks. London: T. & W. Boone.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist gathered from the Gudang man Paida via Kowrarega; the only 'rules' are a vowel-quality key (a as in hard, etc; the print's accents mark vowel quality, not stress) and a note that s/z are wanting in Gudang. Nothing on stress or accent; 'stress' appears only in Latham's rhetorical 'lay considerable stress'.
